outcomes.locator: Overall aim: Developers, Deployers and Integrators

courses.name: Data Science and Applied Machine Learning I
courses.description: Applies supervised and unsupervised analysis, dimensionality reduction and visualization to text, images and scientific data.
courses.prerequisites: (CSCI 1301-1301L or CSCI 1301E or CSCI 1360 or CSCI 1360E or CSCI 1300-1300L or ENGR 1140 or ENGR 1140E or ENGR 1140H or ELEE 2045 or INFO 2000 or INFO 2000E) and (MATH 2250 or MATH 2250E or CSCI 2150-2150L)

courses.name: Data Science and Applied Machine Learning II
courses.description: Studies advanced learning methods, randomized computation and scalable data analysis.
courses.prerequisites: CSCI 3360 or CSCI 3360E or INFO 3000 or INFO 3000E

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduces agents, search, knowledge representation, reasoning, planning and machine learning.
courses.prerequisites: [(CSCI 2610 or CSCI 2610E or CSCI 2611 or PHIL 2500) and (CSCI 1300-1300L or CSCI 1301-1301L or CSCI 1301E)] or permission of department

courses.name: Introduction to Computational Investing
courses.description: Applies computational finance and machine learning to market data and trading strategies.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisite or corequisite: CSCI 2720 or CSCI 2725

courses.name: Data Mining
courses.description: Surveys data-mining methods and their application to complex datasets.

courses.name: Introduction to Robotics
courses.description: Models robotic perception and motion and implements algorithms in simulated environments.

courses.name: Evolutionary Computation and Its Applications
courses.description: Studies evolutionary computation and its use in optimization and AI research.

courses.name: Reinforcement Learning
courses.description: Examines reinforcement learning for single and multiple agents acting under uncertainty.

courses.name: Biomedical Image Analysis
courses.description: Develops algorithms and software for biomedical imaging and image analysis.
courses.prerequisites: CSCI 2720 or CSCI 2725 or permission of department

courses.name: Computational Neuroscience
courses.description: Studies computational models of neural systems and analysis of neural signals.
courses.prerequisites: CSCI 2720 or CSCI 2725 or permission of department

courses.name: Special Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Covers selected advanced computing topics; the AI emphasis requires an approved AI-related topic.

requirements.title: AI emphasis requirements
requirements.summary: Complete the listed required courses and at least the specified number of AI options.

requirements.title: At least 2 AI electives
requirements.summary: This is a minimum selection; further qualifying electives may count toward the parent degree.

requirements.title: Special topics approval
requirements.summary: CSCI 4900/6900 requires prior approval and an artificial-intelligence-related topic.

requirements.title: Conditional parent-degree exceptions
requirements.summary: After all AI emphasis requirements are fulfilled, these parent-degree requirements are waived: CSCI 4720: Computer Architecture and Organization; CSCI 4050/4370: Application Design; CSCI 4730/4760: System Design. All other major requirements remain in force.

requirements.title: Parent major-elective counting
requirements.summary: AI emphasis electives count toward the parent's 12-hour major-elective requirement; do not add them as a second credit total.

requirements.title: CS bachelor degree and accreditation distinction
requirements.summary: This emphasis accompanies a Computer Science bachelor degree. The department states that the modified AI track does not meet ABET accreditation requirements; the regular CS degree is separately described as accredited.

requirements.title: Grade minimum for major-related coursework
requirements.summary: Major-related coursework and associated prerequisites require C (2.0) or higher. This includes the AI emphasis within the CS degree.

notes: Complete designation covers local emphasis requirements and its explicit modifications to the parent CS bachelor plan, not every parent degree requirement.

Published paired undergraduate/graduate numbers and cross-list prefixes are retained as one source-listed course option. This does not establish unrestricted undergraduate access to graduate-numbered sections.
At least two of eight AI electives are required after three fixed courses. CSCI 4900/6900 requires prior approval and an AI topic.

After full emphasis completion, CSCI 4720 and the CSCI 4050/4370 and CSCI 4730/4760 requirement groups are waived. Every other parent major requirement remains in force; emphasis electives also count toward 12 hours of major electives.

The department states that this modified AI track does not meet ABET accreditation requirements. This distinction is separate from the regular CS degree accreditation and is preserved without a quality judgment.
All major-related coursework and prerequisites require C (2.0) or higher. Course metadata is reviewed below; public resources, calendar/unit normalization and catalog edition remain unverified.

The requirements page explicitly dates availability to Fall 2026; the announcement is an earlier approval statement. This supports the source-stated start term; it is not inferred from the older news URL.

Reviewed the eleven course links from the AI emphasis. Undergraduate prerequisite or pre/corequisite labels are preserved separately from graduate prerequisites. Paired undergraduate/graduate codes do not establish undergraduate access to the graduate course. The emphasis labels 4550 as CSCI(PHIL), while its own linked Bulletin record labels it CSCI(ARTI); preserve that source-specific cross-list discrepancy. CSCI 4900/6900 is a variable 1–4 hour topics course, repeatable to a maximum 14 hours; neither range nor repeat maximum is a fixed course amount. Its AI topic requires the existing approval rule. Published hours remain unnormalized. Course-specific learning outcomes are not promoted to program outcomes. The September 30, 2025 announcement says the emphasis is approved; only the requirements page explicitly states availability starting Fall 2026. That is an availability statement, not independent first-enrollment evidence.
